# 01. Planning & Strategy

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Define why the site exists, who it serves, what success means, and what constraints govern every later decision.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A written business objective for the site, expressed as measurable outcomes rather than vague preferences.
- [ ] A primary audience definition with decision stage, pain points, objections, location or market, device expectations, and accessibility needs.
- [ ] A secondary audience definition for influencers, hiring managers, partners, press, repeat visitors, or existing customers where relevant.
- [ ] A value proposition statement that explains the offer, audience, differentiated benefit, and proof standard.
- [ ] A scope boundary that states what the static site will and will not do without backend services.
- [ ] A free and open-source tooling policy covering build tools, libraries, analytics, fonts, icons, image processing, and testing.
- [ ] A success metric model for leads, calls, bookings, downloads, inquiries, newsletter signups, portfolio views, content engagement, or local actions.
- [ ] A content inventory or content gap register for all required pages, assets, claims, proof points, and legal notices.
- [ ] A launch risk register covering brand, content, accessibility, SEO, analytics, legal, hosting, DNS, and client approval risks.
- [ ] A page priority map that separates launch-critical pages from post-launch enhancements.

## Must Be True
- [ ] The strategy must fit a static front-end architecture without assuming server sessions, private databases, server-rendered personalization, or paid form processors.
- [ ] Every primary page must have one clear user job and one primary business outcome.
- [ ] The target audience must be specific enough to guide content tone, information order, proof selection, and interaction density.
- [ ] Site goals must include quality goals, not only traffic goals: accessibility, performance, maintainability, privacy, and content accuracy.
- [ ] The project must define what counts as done before design and development decisions are judged.
- [ ] Stakeholder preferences must not override measurable user needs, legal requirements, or accessibility requirements.
- [ ] Premium positioning must be supported by proof, clarity, speed, polish, and trust signals rather than decorative complexity.
- [ ] The plan must include maintenance ownership after launch for content, dependencies, forms, analytics, and hosting records.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Confirm that every proposed feature can run as static HTML/CSS/JS or through an explicitly approved free-tier-friendly service.
- [ ] Confirm that no required business process depends on a paid website builder, proprietary plugin, or closed export format.
- [ ] Confirm that the site map covers all essential user journeys and all required legal, privacy, and contact pages.
- [ ] Confirm that tracking requirements are compatible with the privacy consent model and jurisdictions served.
- [ ] Confirm that multilingual, local, or content-heavy requirements are planned before URL architecture is frozen.
- [ ] Confirm that visual ambition does not threaten page speed, readability, accessibility, or maintainability.
- [ ] Confirm that the client can maintain the chosen content workflow without vendor lock-in.
- [ ] Confirm that launch measurement includes baseline capture and post-launch review dates.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid strategy based only on competitor imitation, design trends, or stakeholder taste.
- [ ] Avoid promising backend behavior such as accounts, dashboards, real-time inventory, private submissions, or payments unless a compliant external service is explicitly scoped.
- [ ] Avoid vague objectives such as modernize the website without measurable acceptance standards.
- [ ] Avoid tool choices that make source files unavailable, unreadable, or non-portable.
- [ ] Avoid content plans that depend on missing testimonials, unverified claims, fake scarcity, or unsupported awards.
- [ ] Avoid launching without a maintenance owner and a rollback path.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The strategy must make prioritization obvious when scope, budget, or timing changes.
- [ ] Every checklist category must have an owner and acceptance evidence.
- [ ] The site must be understandable, credible, fast, accessible, and conversion-ready before visual embellishment is considered complete.
- [ ] The planning file must be usable as a launch decision record months after the project ends.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the audit script to verify that required static files, page types, and metadata exist before launch.
- [ ] Use generated reports as evidence, not as a replacement for strategy sign-off.
- [ ] Keep site configuration in a plain JSON file so the audit can run without paid project management tools.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Project definition: purpose, static-site fit, constraints, budget, timeline, integrations, content, launch requirements, and maintenance plan.
- [ ] Business strategy: positioning, offer clarity, audience, competitive advantage, conversion route, trust goals, revenue or authority goals, SEO goals, analytics goals, and maintenance goals.
- [ ] Audience strategy: primary and secondary audiences, knowledge level, pain points, objections, motivations, trust needs, preferred contact methods, devices, and user intent.
- [ ] User journeys: first-time, returning, high-intent, low-intent, mobile, search, social, referral, blog reader, contact-ready, post-submit, and 404 recovery journeys.
- [ ] Competitive strategy: reviewed competitors, industry expectations, common conversion patterns, trust signals, SEO topics, weaknesses, design cliches, and differentiation opportunities.
- [ ] Scope planning: page scope, section scope, feature scope, excluded features, forms, CTAs, floating actions, accessibility controls, analytics events, and no filler pages or sections.
- [ ] Free/open-source rule: no paid builders, paid plugins, paid overlays, paid analytics, paid lock-in, or hidden proprietary dependency for core static-site functionality.
- [ ] Information architecture planning: page hierarchy, navigation strategy, content grouping, footer grouping, internal links, growth paths, and legal/utility page placement.
- [ ] Page and section strategy: homepage, about, service, solution, contact, hero, proof, FAQ, final CTA, section purpose, section flow, and section variety.
- [ ] Content strategy: required copy, images, videos, testimonials, case studies, FAQs, legal text, metadata, alt text, content hierarchy, truthfulness, originality, and source ownership.
- [ ] Brand, UX, UI, SEO, accessibility, performance, analytics, compliance, asset, form, conversion, multilingual, blog, portfolio, static selling, integration, security, documentation, QA, launch, and maintenance plans are defined before build.
- [ ] Strategic red flags are resolved: unclear offer, no proof, too many pages, backend-only requirements, paid dependency pressure, sensitive data collection, unclear ownership, and no maintenance plan.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
